frequency_question: How often do required statutory strike notice periods and procedural steps fit entirely within a 12-day window?
membership_rule: Includes any organized labor action requiring mandatory conciliation, voting, and formal notice periods before commencement; excludes spontaneous or wildcat strikes.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named instances analyzed; structurally all formal legal strike processes exceed the 12-day threshold.
known_gaps: Assuming all steps run concurrently rather than sequentially still violates the 12-day ceiling.
skeleton: Standard labor dispute process skeleton: Conciliation meetings (min 14 days) + Ballot tabulation (7 days) + Statutory notice period (14 to 30 days).
multiplier: 12 available days divided by minimum required procedural timeline of roughly 35 days.
validity_reason: Labor laws and statutory notice periods governing industrial disputes change very slowly over decades.
